{{Quote|Nicknamed the mouse droid, the MSE is a nimble courier that delivers secure point-to-point communiqués. MSEs are also used for simple maintenance tasks including floor polishing and spot welding. If you see these droids zip by, give them a wide berth. It is best not to interfere with its high-priority delivery.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''|<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
The '''MSE-6 series repair droid''', sometimes referred to as the '''mouse droid''', was a small, box-shaped, wheeled general purpose [[MSE-series]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] often used for delivery and maintenance purposes.<ref name="Handbook" /> MSE-6 units were most notably on [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and both [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] during the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Specifications==
[[File:Mse6droid.jpg|thumb|left|A chain of MSE-6 [[Droid/Legends|droids]].]]
The MSE-6 stood about 25 centimeters tall and ran on four wheels. Although programmed with multiple capabilities, the droid was designed with only a singular function. A modular circuit matrix was installed beneath the droid's boxy shell, and contained programming for one skill. Commonly, mouse droids carried out cleanup and basic repair duties, and could serve in security and communications fields. Since each droid possessed only a single skill, multiple mouse droids could chain together to pool their resources for more complex assignments. Trains of MSE-6 droids could often be seen guiding troops through military installations; this kind of duty required mouse droids to be programmed with complete readouts of their assigned areas. In addition, due to their use in military outposts, MSE-6 units were rigged to melt down if captured, giving the droids a strong self-preservation instinct.

==History==
{{Quote|Lastly, we have a complaint from the Aar'aa regarding their order. Apparently, the MSE droids skittering underfoot are making them uncomfortably&hellip; hungry.|[[Rebaxan Columni/Legends|Rebaxan Columni]] executives, product testing the MSE-6|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
The MSE-6 was developed by the [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]] at [[Rebaxan Columni/Legends|Rebaxan Columni]]. Rebaxan produced billions of the droids, heavily promoting them in over four hundred [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] and marketing them as "cute"; the general public instead considered them irritating, and some considered them similar to annoying vermin. Many MSE-6 droids were used by the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] also maintained a number of these droids and [[MSE-4/Legends|MSE-4]] droids, a similar but smaller model, in the [[Separatist Council war room/Legends|Separatist Council War Room]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] at the end of the Clone Wars.

[[File:MSE-6_Mouse_Droid.jpg|thumb|A MSE-6 'Mouse' droid]]
Rebaxan Columni became desperate to sell the massive collection of droids they had built, so they sold the entire lot of them to the Empire for work in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], which was desperate for droids, before bankruptcy. MSE-6s became common on the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].

[[Gara Petothel]] and her [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droid]] [[Tonin]] used the MSE-6 droids of [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]]'s [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] [[Iron Fist (Executor-class)|''Iron Fist'']] to attempt to destroy it by reprogramming them and replacing their wheels with magnetic strips. The droids severely damaged the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], trapping the vessel at the [[Selaggis system/Legends|Selaggis system]] so that [[General/Legends|General]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] could come and [[Battle of Selaggis|engage it]]. She also used the droids to alter holocam feeds, hack into the ship's main computer, and gain access to restricted levels of the ship.

A while later, at the height of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] modified a number of mouse droids into [[YVH-M]] droids, which served as mobile surveillance units to root out infiltrators on [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]].

The MSE-6 droids in [[137 ABY]] were stationed on the planet [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]].

==Behind the scenes==
The MSE-6-series repair droid first appeared in the film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>. The droid was tested by production designers on [[March 15]], [[1976]], where it was dubbed "baby box." The test run of the droid was filmed by cameraman [[Gilbert Taylor]] and directed by [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Empire of Dreams">''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>
